transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time (UTC): 2027-11-12 16:00 - 17:00 UTC | Duration: 54 minutes | Recorded: yes
Attendees: Alex Kim (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (Nimbus), Priya Anand (Nimbus), Marcus Bennett (Nimbus)

Summary:
- Discovery focused on embedding dimensionality, quantization tradeoffs, hybrid routing between vector DB and reranker, and hosting options (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private VPC).
- Customer wants predictable tail latency at 50-200 QPS for search API, and cost targets per query.
- Next step: Redwood to provide Dedicated pilot pricing and benchmark kit; Nimbus to share sample queries and embedding stats.

Topics:
- Current infra & vector DB stack (self-hosted Milvus currently)
- Embedding dims and potential quantization (8-bit/4-bit)
- Hybrid routing: top-k fanout to vector DB then rerank with LLM on Redwood Hosted/Dedicated
- Private/VPC options and audit requirements (SOC2 + ISO requested)

Action items (short list):
- See metadata action_items above for owners and due dates.

Questions raised:
- How does Redwood handle KV cache with quantized models?
- What is expected degradation in rerank quality when using 8-bit vs 4-bit embeddings?
- Options for per-route cost controls and burst capacity?

Transcript body:
[00:00] Alex (Redwood AE): All right, hey everyone, thanks for joining — I think we're at 16:00 UTC, appreciate you making time. Quick intros?
[00:08] Jordan (Nimbus): Hi, Jordan here — head of search and relevance at Nimbus. Uh Priya's on infra, Marcus is our CTO.
[00:12] Priya (Nimbus): Hi all.
[00:13] Marcus (Nimbus): Hey.
[00:14] Samir (Redwood SE): Samir, I'm the solutions engineer on the account, happy to dig into perf and benchmarks today.
[00:18] Alex: Cool, scope for today is embeddings + routing model for search, quantization options, and hosting tradeoffs — hosted, dedicated, or private VPC.
[00:24] Jordan: Yeah, our immediate driver is cost and tail latency. We've got a 2M doc index, queries are bursty — baseline 50 QPS average but spikes to 200 QPS for short windows, and 95th latency needs to be under 300ms for the search API.
[00:40] Priya: Security is a hard requirement. We need SOC2, ISO, and audit logs; for long term we might need VPC/private deployment. But we'd like to start with a faster path to value.
[00:50] Alex: Great. Quick question on your current stack — what are you using for vector storage and rerank?
[00:55] Jordan: We're running Milvus on-prem in k8s for vectors, FAISS sharding, and we do rescoring with a small BERT reranker on CPU — slow. Cost's high.
[01:08] Samir: Right. So common pattern is to do a top-k fanout from Milvus, then rerank with an LLM. Redwood can host the reranker and support either hosted embeddings generation or you can bring embeddings produced in-house. Important tradeoffs: embedding dim, quantization, and where you place the rerank.
[01:26] Marcus: We're evaluating the economics of doing embedding generation ourselves vs using API. Also curious about quantizing embeddings and model size — how much quality loss do we accept if we go 8-bit or 4-bit?
[01:36] Samir: For embeddings specifically, quantization of embedding vectors (not model weights) like product quantization or PQ reduces vector size with controlled recall drop. For model weights quantization when serving reranker, 8-bit weights usually keep quality close; 4-bit can introduce more variance depending on model and prompts. There's also hybrid: keep embeddings high-dim but quantize on-disk in the vector DB and use Redwood's hosted rerank for final scoring.
[01:55] Jordan: Ok. Our current embedding dim is 1024, vector size is heavy. We're exploring compact dims 384 or 512 to save ops.
[02:03] Priya: Right now we store floats32, so footprint is big — storage and IO on Milvus is the cost.
[02:10] Samir: Sounds familiar. We typically recommend: for throughput-first pipelines, 384-512 dims with PQ or OPQ in the VDB, plus a 64-128 token rerank call. For very low-latency SLOs you can move reranker to Dedicated instances to keep tail latency predictable.
[02:27] Alex: Can you share a rough QPS distribution? Like percentiles?
[02:31] Jordan: Median 30 QPS, p95 is 180 during peak windows, p99 unknown but we'd like under 500ms.
[02:38] Alex: Good. For Dedicated we offer reserved pools that avoid noisy neighbor issues. You get predictable throughput and our autoscaling policies can be tuned for burst windows.
[02:48] Marcus: What's the typical cost delta between Hosted and Dedicated for this workload?
[02:52] Alex: It depends on commit and utilization. Ballpark: Hosted for small scale is higher per-token but zero infra ops. Dedicated with commitments can halve unit cost at sustained load, and Private/VPC adds a platform fee. We'll send concrete tiers in the follow-up.
[03:06] Priya: About VPC — do you support customer-managed KMS, audit logs to our SIEM, and private endpoints?
[03:14] Samir: Yes, Private supports customer KMS/HSM integration and direct VPC peering. Audit logs can be exported to your S3 or SIEM; we'll share the security pack. In Hosted there's also retention controls and audit traces, but for strict compliance Private is the usual path.
[03:29] Jordan: On rerank latency: what's the expected latency for a 128-token rerank on Dedicated GPUs?
[03:36] Samir: Typical is 30-80ms per call for modern optimized runtimes on A100/H100-class GPUs if you have batching. For single-shot low batch, tail can be higher. That's why we introduced continuous batching and KV cache techniques — to reduce per-token overhead.
[03:52] Jordan: Can you explain KV cache in plain terms? Our infra folks keep hearing KV cash (laughs).
[03:58] Samir: (laughs) Yeah, KV cache, not cash. It's the key/value cache used during autoregressive decoding. For rerank models we often do full scoring, which benefits less from decoding cache, but for chat-style rerank or contextualized rerank it helps. Important point: with quantized model weights the runtime still manages KV and tensor types; there can be small perf differences.
[04:20] Priya: Is Redwood's runtime compatible with our on-prem Milvus or do you recommend moving vectors into Redwood's managed vector store?
[04:28] Samir: We can work with either. For hybrid routing, typical flow: query hits your API -> call to VDB (Milvus) for top-K -> pass candidate doc ids and contexts to Redwood rerank endpoint. Alternatively we can host the VDB close to the Dedicated pool for lower network hop. We also support an optional prefetching cache to reduce VDB calls.
[04:47] Jordan: Do you have benchmarks for fanout sizes? We're trying to decide between top-100 then rerank or smaller top-20 with denser embeddings.
[04:55] Samir: We usually recommend top-50 as a starting point. If embedding dims are lower and recall drops, you can increase fanout. There's a cost vs latency trade — larger fanout increases rerank compute and round trips. We'll include a benchmark script so you can try top-20/50/100 with your queries.
[05:12] Marcus: On quantization — we don't want surprises in semantic recall. Can Redwood run an A/B eval with our ground truth?
[05:18] Alex: Absolutely. Samir can instrument the benchmark with your relevance labels and run recall/MRR comparisons across dims and PQ profiles. That will give a clear delta between 32-bit vs PQ-compressed vectors and between 8-bit vs 4-bit model weights for reranking.
[05:32] Priya: Operationally, what's the rollout? If we start with Hosted for rerank and still keep Milvus on-prem, later migrate rerank to Dedicated — is that seamless?
[05:41] Alex: The API and routing layer are the same. You can pin routes to Hosted initially and then switch the route to Dedicated with canary rollout and rollback. Same prompts, same model versions.
[05:52] Jordan: One more question: burst windows to 200 QPS — can you tell us how autoscaling behaves? Will cold starts impact tail?
[05:59] Samir: Autoscaling has two pieces: instance scaling and warm pool/burst. For Dedicated we provision warm capacity and you can enable instant burst to avoid cold starts. Warm pools reduce tail on scale-up. We'll propose autoscale thresholds in the pilot config.
[06:14] Jordan: Do you offer an SLA for p95 latency?
[06:18] Alex: Dedicated customers can get latency-backed SLAs; Hosted has uptime SLAs and best-effort latency guarantees. We'll include SLA options in the follow-up.
[06:27] Priya: On security pack — please include details on key rotation and hsm support. Also need info about data deletion and retention.
[06:35] Alex: We'll attach the SOC2/ISO pack and the data retention docs.
[06:40] Marcus: How much engineering effort to integrate the benchmark? What do you need from us?
[06:44] Samir: Ideally: a 100k sample of indexed vectors (or direct access to Milvus snapshot), a set of 1k queries with relevance labels or clicks, and a small test account for API keys. We'll run the script and share metrics.
[06:57] Jordan: Sounds doable. We'll anonymize and share.
[07:01] Alex: Great. Let me summarize next steps quickly. Alex will send pricing for Dedicated pilot and burst options; Samir will drop the benchmark kit, sample dataset, and instructions; Nimbus will share query samples and embedding stats; we reconvene after benchmark results.
[07:14] Jordan: Perfect. Quick operational question — if we go Private later, any scheduling lead time?
[07:19] Samir: Private deployments typically have a setup lead time — depends on region and connectivity, usually 4-6 weeks for a fully private VPC/on-prem package; can be faster for a VPC peering-only arrangement. We'll detail this in the follow-up.
[07:34] Marcus: One last thing — competitors: we're also talking to Pinecone and a vendor running Milvus managed. Curious how you compare on cost predictability.
[07:43] Alex: Pinecone is vector-store focused; Redwood is routing + rerank + hosting — our differentiation is end-to-end serving with predictable inference economics and fallback routing. We'll add a short competitive note in our follow-up.
[07:58] Jordan: Ok thanks.
[08:00] Alex: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up by Monday with the materials.

(End of recording)
